blocks.content: Unlike a Deployment, which creates every replica in parallel, a StatefulSet creates its Pods one at a time, in strict order, each one must be running and ready before the next is even started.
When a StatefulSet is first created, its Pods do not all appear at once, app-0 is created first, then app-1, then app-2, in that exact order, every single time.

blocks.alt: One Pod at a time, always in the same ascending order

blocks.content: 2. Each Must Be Ready Before the Next Starts
blocks.text: 2. Each Must Be Ready Before the Next Starts

blocks.content: It is not just about creation order, the previous Pod must reach a running and ready state (covered in the Health Checks module) before the next one is even started, a genuine gate, not just a scheduling suggestion.

blocks.alt: A real, enforced gate, not just a loose creation order

blocks.content: This is a meaningful departure from how a Deployment behaves, covered in its own module, a Deployment creates all of its replicas in parallel, with no ordering guarantee whatsoever, StatefulSet's strict sequencing is a deliberate, different choice.

blocks.alt: Parallel and unordered versus strict, deliberate sequencing

blocks.content: For many stateful systems, this ordering reflects a genuine dependency, a database's leader or primary instance often needs to exist and be ready before replica instances can meaningfully join and start replicating from it.

blocks.alt: A genuine dependency, not an arbitrary rule, for many real stateful systems

blocks.content: 5. Opting Out, When You Genuinely Need To
blocks.text: 5. Opting Out, When You Genuinely Need To

blocks.content: For workloads that do not actually need this ordering, podManagementPolicy: Parallel is an explicit opt-out, creating Pods concurrently instead, worth reaching for deliberately, not as a default, since the ordering exists for a reason in most stateful use cases.

blocks.alt: An explicit, deliberate opt-out, available when the ordering genuinely is not needed

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A StatefulSet creates its Pods strictly one at a time, in ascending order, each one must be running and ready before the next even starts.
This reflects a genuine dependency in many stateful systems (a leader existing before replicas join), and podManagementPolicy: Parallel is the explicit opt-out when it is not needed.
